jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Mine Geologist directs day-to-day ore and waste routing for the Company’s open pit mining operations, accurately classifying and dispatching mined material to the leach pad, waste dump, or stockpile. This role collects and interprets blast hole and leach pad sample data, runs grade interpolation against the block model in Micromine, and applies cut-off grade and blend logic to maximize recoverable ounces while protecting leach performance. The Mine Geologist works daily with Mine Operations, Survey, and the Metallurgy/Process team, and reports to the Geology Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Ore Control & Grade Classification

Perform daily ore and waste routing for all mined material against the current dig block sequence.
Import assay/PXRF results into Micromine and run grade interpolation against the block model.
Apply cut-off grade and blend logic to classify ore/waste and assign material to leach pad, waste dump, or stockpile.
QC check grade control results against the resource model for the same blocks and flag discrepancies beyond agreed tolerance.

Sampling & Geological Logging

Collect or supervise blast hole and leach pad sampling per site protocol (spacing, depth increments, contamination control).
Run field PXRF readings where applicable and log results against hole/sample ID, flagging holes requiring lab confirmation.
Log lithology, oxidation state, and leachability flags (clay content, hardness, weathering) that directly affect heap leach performance and blend decisions.
Validate blast hole/sample collar coordinates against survey pickup before finalizing sample locations.

Data Management & Reporting

Input geological data into the database daily and continually monitor database accuracy.
Update the grade control database with finalized block classifications.
Deliver a daily production/reconciliation update to Mine Planning and Ops on tonnes/grade mined vs. plan, and any deviations.
Track and report drill program footages via Daily Shift Reports.

Drill Planning & Geological Mapping

Generate drillhole plans to efficiently define ore extents and grade.
Generate geological maps and sections to support modeling and drill planning.
Log drillholes and sample along geological boundaries.

Dispatch & Cross-Functional Communication

Issue dig plans/ore polygons to Survey and Mine Ops for pit marking (flagging, GPS guidance for dozers/loaders).
Communicate blend recommendations to the Metallurgy/Process team, particularly material with elevated clay or hardness likely to affect leach kinetics.
Provide end-of-shift handover notes on outstanding sample results, pending lab turnarounds, and any pit access or geotechnical concerns.

Safety & Environmental Stewardship

Place the safety, health, and wellbeing of employees and contractors as the top priority in all field activity.
Identify and control occupational hazards; support the Company’s safety programs through training and field risk assessments.
Train and direct employees on applicable environmental permits and best management practices, and report opportunities to minimize environmental impact

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor of Science in Geology or Geological Engineering.
1-3 years of experience in ore/grade control within a mining operation; fully competent at this experience level.
Working proficiency in Micromine (or comparable software such as Vulcan or Leapfrog).
Working knowledge of PXRF field analysis and grade interpolation techniques.
Ability to work and live onsite at a remote mining operation.

﻿

Preferred

Master’s degree in Geology.
Heap leach or oxide gold experience, including leachability logging (clay content, hardness, weathering).
Experience interfacing directly with metallurgy/process teams on blend recommendations.

Position Summary

The Senior Exploration Geologist leads near-mine resource conversion drilling around the pit envelope, advancing Inferred resources to Indicated through RC and diamond infill and extensional programs. This role owns pit-wall and near-pit structural mapping that underpins resource model confidence and structural domain control and directly supervises field technicians and samplers on logging quality, sample chain of custody, and field HSE conduct. The Exploration Geologist works closely with Grade Control, Mine Planning, and Survey to keep near-pit drilling and mapping aligned with the active mining schedule, reporting to the Geology Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Resource Conversion Drilling & Field Supervision

Direct RC and diamond infill/extensional drilling programs to convert Inferred resources to Indicated around the pit envelope.
Supervise field technicians and samplers daily, including logging QA, sample chain of custody, and field HSE conduct.
Review overnight drill progress each shift (meters, hole status, downtime reasons) and action issues before the day’s program proceeds.
Confirm daily rig targets, mapping traverses, and site access with Mine Planning and Survey at shift start.

Structural Mapping & Geological Interpretation

Conduct and review pit-wall and near-pit structural mapping (veins, alteration, shear fabric, contacts) using orogenic-style structural criteria.
Spot-check core/chip logging quality in the field against established structural and geological standards.
Update structural/geological interpretation and domains as new logging and mapping data become available.

Data Management & QAQC

Review Geobank data entry daily (collar, downhole survey, lithology/structural logs) for completeness and error flags.
Confirm QAQC insertion (CRM/blank/duplicate) at the correct frequency before samples leave site.
Import and validate weekly assay results into Geobank; reconcile against QAQC performance and flag failures for re-assay or resample, routing sign-off to the Geology Manager.

Resource Modeling & Reporting

Incorporate validated monthly assay and structural data into the Micromine Mineral Resource model.
Track and report Inferred → Indicated conversion status against the resource conversion plan.
Compile and present weekly drilling/QAQC ops updates and a monthly geology report (resource conversion progress, drilling summary vs. budget, QAQC compliance, structural/model changes, and risks to resource classification) to the Geology Manager.

Team & Program Planning

Roster field technicians and samplers weekly and align drill targeting with resource/mine planning input.
Review field crew performance, logging quality trends, and training needs; develop the next month’s drill program and mapping plan against budget.
Attend weekly ops meetings with the Geology Manager, Grade Control, Mine Planning, and Survey to align drilling and mapping access with the mining schedule.

Safety & Environmental Stewardship

Place the safety, health, and wellbeing of employees and contractors as the top priority in all field activity.
Identify and control occupational hazards; conduct field risk assessments and safety observations.
Support the Company’s commitment to environmental stewardship and comply with all applicable permits and best management practices.

Bachelor of Science in Geology or Geological Engineering.
5+ years of experience in resource or exploration geology within a mining operation.
Working proficiency in Micromine (or comparable resource modeling software such as Vulcan or Leapfrog).

Ability to work and live onsite at a remote mining operation.

Position Summary

The Mine Geologist directs day-to-day ore and waste routing for the Company’s open pit mining operations, accurately classifying and dispatching mined material to the leach pad, waste dump, or stockpile. This role collects and interprets blast hole and leach pad sample data, runs grade interpolation against the block model in Micromine, and applies cut-off grade and blend logic to maximize recoverable ounces while protecting leach performance. The Mine Geologist works daily with Mine Operations, Survey, and the Metallurgy/Process team, and reports to the Geology Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Ore Control & Grade Classification

Perform daily ore and waste routing for all mined material against the current dig block sequence.
Import assay/PXRF results into Micromine and run grade interpolation against the block model.
Apply cut-off grade and blend logic to classify ore/waste and assign material to leach pad, waste dump, or stockpile.
QC check grade control results against the resource model for the same blocks and flag discrepancies beyond agreed tolerance.

Sampling & Geological Logging

Collect or supervise blast hole and leach pad sampling per site protocol (spacing, depth increments, contamination control).
Run field PXRF readings where applicable and log results against hole/sample ID, flagging holes requiring lab confirmation.
Log lithology, oxidation state, and leachability flags (clay content, hardness, weathering) that directly affect heap leach performance and blend decisions.
Validate blast hole/sample collar coordinates against survey pickup before finalizing sample locations.

Data Management & Reporting

Input geological data into the database daily and continually monitor database accuracy.
Update the grade control database with finalized block classifications.
Deliver a daily production/reconciliation update to Mine Planning and Ops on tonnes/grade mined vs. plan, and any deviations.
Track and report drill program footages via Daily Shift Reports.

Drill Planning & Geological Mapping

Generate drillhole plans to efficiently define ore extents and grade.
Generate geological maps and sections to support modeling and drill planning.
Log drillholes and sample along geological boundaries.

Dispatch & Cross-Functional Communication

Issue dig plans/ore polygons to Survey and Mine Ops for pit marking (flagging, GPS guidance for dozers/loaders).
Communicate blend recommendations to the Metallurgy/Process team, particularly material with elevated clay or hardness likely to affect leach kinetics.
Provide end-of-shift handover notes on outstanding sample results, pending lab turnarounds, and any pit access or geotechnical concerns.

The Senior Exploration Geologist leads near-mine resource conversion drilling around the pit envelope, advancing Inferred resources to Indicated through RC and diamond infill and extensional programs. This role owns pit-wall and near-pit structural mapping that underpins resource model confidence and structural domain control and directly supervises field technicians and samplers on logging quality, sample chain of custody, and field HSE conduct. The Exploration Geologist works closely with Grade Control, Mine Planning, and Survey to keep near-pit drilling and mapping aligned with the active mining schedule, reporting to the Geology Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Resource Conversion Drilling & Field Supervision

Direct RC and diamond infill/extensional drilling programs to convert Inferred resources to Indicated around the pit envelope.
Supervise field technicians and samplers daily, including logging QA, sample chain of custody, and field HSE conduct.
Review overnight drill progress each shift (meters, hole status, downtime reasons) and action issues before the day’s program proceeds.
Confirm daily rig targets, mapping traverses, and site access with Mine Planning and Survey at shift start.

Structural Mapping & Geological Interpretation

Conduct and review pit-wall and near-pit structural mapping (veins, alteration, shear fabric, contacts) using orogenic-style structural criteria.
Spot-check core/chip logging quality in the field against established structural and geological standards.
Update structural/geological interpretation and domains as new logging and mapping data become available.

Data Management & QAQC

Review Geobank data entry daily (collar, downhole survey, lithology/structural logs) for completeness and error flags.
Confirm QAQC insertion (CRM/blank/duplicate) at the correct frequency before samples leave site.
Import and validate weekly assay results into Geobank; reconcile against QAQC performance and flag failures for re-assay or resample, routing sign-off to the Geology Manager.

Resource Modeling & Reporting

Incorporate validated monthly assay and structural data into the Micromine Mineral Resource model.
Track and report Inferred → Indicated conversion status against the resource conversion plan.
Compile and present weekly drilling/QAQC ops updates and a monthly geology report (resource conversion progress, drilling summary vs. budget, QAQC compliance, structural/model changes, and risks to resource classification) to the Geology Manager.

Team & Program Planning

Roster field technicians and samplers weekly and align drill targeting with resource/mine planning input.
Review field crew performance, logging quality trends, and training needs; develop the next month’s drill program and mapping plan against budget.
Attend weekly ops meetings with the Geology Manager, Grade Control, Mine Planning, and Survey to align drilling and mapping access with the mining schedule.

Safety & Environmental Stewardship

Place the safety, health, and wellbeing of employees and contractors as the top priority in all field activity.
Identify and control occupational hazards; conduct field risk assessments and safety observations.
Support the Company’s commitment to environmental stewardship and comply with all applicable permits and best management practices.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor of Science in Geology or Geological Engineering.
5+ years of experience in resource or exploration geology within a mining operation.
Working proficiency in Micromine (or comparable resource modeling software such as Vulcan or Leapfrog).
Demonstrated knowledge of QAQC protocols (CRM/blank/duplicate insertion and review).
Ability to work and live onsite at a remote mining operation.

Preferred

Master’s degree in Geology.
Experience with orogenic-style gold mineralization and structural domain interpretation.
Prior experience supervising field technicians or samplers.
